subject: microbiology
title: Borrelia burgdorferi, Lyme Disease, Erythema Migrans and Borrelia recurrentis

steps.tx: **Borrelia burgdorferi** sensu lato is a tick borne spirochaete complex transmitted mainly by Ixodes ticks after prolonged attachment. It causes Lyme disease in North America and Europe, with genospecies differing in tissue preference. The organism is difficult to culture in routine laboratories, requiring special Barbour Stoenner Kelly medium, so serology, PCR in selected specimens and clinical recognition dominate diagnosis.
steps.say: Lyme disease is transmitted during prolonged Ixodes feeding and is usually diagnosed clinically or serologically.

left.title: Transmission
points: Ixodes nymphs are small and easily missed
Risk increases after roughly thirty six to forty eight hours attachment
Deer support adult ticks but rodents are key reservoirs
Prompt tick removal reduces risk

right.title: Complex members
points: B burgdorferi sensu stricto prominent in North America
B afzelii associated with skin disease in Europe
B garinii associated more with neuroborreliosis
All are extracellular motile spirochaetes

steps.tx: **Erythema migrans** is the characteristic expanding annular rash of early localised Lyme disease, often with central clearing but frequently uniformly erythematous. It is a clinical diagnosis in an endemic exposure setting, and serology may still be negative. Multiple lesions can indicate early dissemination rather than multiple bites. Photographing and marking the edge can document expansion when the history is uncertain.
steps.say: An expanding erythema migrans lesion in Lyme country should be treated without waiting for serology.

left.title: Typical lesion
points: Expands over days to weeks
Often larger than five centimetres
Minimal scaling or pain
May have central clearing but need not look like a target

right.title: Lookalikes
points: Cellulitis is more painful and rapidly progressive
Tinea has scale and slower change
Granuloma annulare lacks recent expansion
Southern tick associated rash illness can mimic it

steps.tx: Early disseminated Lyme disease may involve **multiple erythema migrans lesions**, facial nerve palsy, lymphocytic meningitis, radiculoneuritis and carditis with fluctuating atrioventricular block. Late disease classically causes intermittent or persistent large joint arthritis, especially the knee, and acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans in European infection. Objective manifestations guide serologic interpretation because nonspecific fatigue and pain alone have very low predictive value.
steps.say: Facial palsy, heart block and a swollen knee are stronger Lyme clues than fatigue alone.

left.title: Neurologic and cardiac
points: Unilateral or bilateral facial palsy
Lymphocytic meningitis
Painful radiculoneuritis, especially in Europe
High degree AV block can fluctuate rapidly

right.title: Late features
points: Recurrent large joint swelling
Acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans
Peripheral neuropathy in late European disease
Objective arthritis usually strongly seropositive

steps.tx: Lyme serology uses a **two tier strategy**: a sensitive enzyme immunoassay first, followed by immunoblot or a second immunoassay in modified two tier protocols. IgM immunoblot interpretation is restricted to early disease because false positives become common when used indiscriminately. Antibodies persist after successful therapy and cannot be used as a test of cure. Pre test probability determines whether a positive result is meaningful.
steps.say: Lyme antibodies record exposure and immune response, not bacterial eradication after treatment.

steps.tx: **Borrelia recurrentis** causes louse borne relapsing fever. It changes surface variable major proteins by gene conversion, temporarily escaping antibody control and producing repeated febrile episodes separated by apparent recovery. The human body louse transmits it in settings of crowding, displacement and poor clothing hygiene. A single antibiotic dose can trigger a Jarisch Herxheimer reaction as organisms are rapidly cleared.
steps.say: Relapsing fever returns because Borrelia changes its surface coat faster than immunity clears it.

vis.alt: Relapsing fever spirochaetes in blood smear
vis.caption: Spirochaetes visible in blood during a febrile relapsing fever episode.

steps.tx: Doxycycline treats most **early Lyme disease** and also covers several tick borne coinfections, while ceftriaxone is used for selected neurologic and high degree cardiac manifestations. Avoid repeating antibiotics for persistent nonspecific symptoms without objective evidence, because prolonged courses add harm without treating a proven ongoing infection. Tick removal, exposure prevention and checking for additional attached ticks complete the encounter.
steps.say: Treat objective Lyme disease decisively, but do not let persistent antibodies justify indefinite antibiotics.

left.title: Usually doxycycline
points: Erythema migrans
Facial palsy without meningitis in selected cases
Mild carditis as outpatient only if appropriate
Early disseminated multiple lesions

right.title: Escalate evaluation
points: Meningitis or radiculoneuritis may require IV therapy by guideline
High degree AV block needs cardiac monitoring
Arthritis may need repeat oral or IV course
Pregnancy and young children need regimen adjustment
